episodes.title: NXIVM Whistleblower Sarah Edmondson: The Vow, DOS Branding & Cult Warning Signs
episodes.description:
Sarah Edmondson, the NXIVM survivor and whistleblower featured in HBO’s The Vow, joins me to reveal how NXIVM manipulated its members, what really happened inside the secret women’s group DOS and why even intelligent, successful people can miss the warning signs of a cult.

As someone who watched The Vow through the eyes of both a pop-culture obsessive and a girl completely fascinated by cults, I can think of no better person to help answer the question so many of us have: How does someone get pulled into a cult and would we realize it if it were happening to us or our children?

Sarah spent 12 years inside NXIVM. She became a leader, ran its Vancouver center and recruited people into an organization she genuinely believed was helping them. After being branded during a DOS initiation ceremony, Sarah left NXIVM and helped expose Keith Raniere and the organization’s abuse.

In this conversation, we discuss:

• How NXIVM presented itself as a self-improvement organization
• Why Sarah joined and why she stayed for 12 years
• Keith Raniere, DOS and NXIVM’s master-slave hierarchy
• Collateral, coercive control and the branding ceremony
• How NXIVM taught members to distrust their own instincts
• The warning signs that “a little bit culty” has become dangerous
• Why smart people are vulnerable to manipulation
• How to help someone involved in a high-control group
• What parents should teach kids about influence and coercion
• Sarah’s life and healing after NXIVM

Sarah is the author of Scarred, co-host of the podcast A Little Bit Culty with her husband, Anthony “Nippy” Ames, and co-author of A Little Bit Culty: Navigating Cults, Control and Coercion.

Subscribe to Shut Up! Tell Me More for candid conversations with reality-TV personalities, pop-culture figures and wildly interesting people.

This episode includes discussions of coercive control, sexual exploitation, abuse and branding.
